Jordan (eng): Thanks for the talk — quick follow-ups from the team. Two quick asks: 1) how narrow vs broad should our mission be when we talk to customers (serve best inference vs build ML stack)? 2) who do we call our core competitor when we pitch to platform teams?

Morgan (CEO): Great q's. Short answers first: mission language should emphasize 'serving' as the differentiator — operationalizing inference reliably and cheaply. For customers that care about model R&D we still support model choices, but we lead with predictable production outcomes. Competitors: it's different by buyer — for startups it's primarily LLM API vendors, for platform teams it's inference infra vendors + major cloud endpoints.

Priya (Head of Product): To add — product framing matters by motion. For PLG self-serve landing page, highlight low friction + predictable cost. For enterprise outreach, lead with SLA, VPC/private deployment, auditability. We should avoid saying "we do everything" — be explicit about solving serving economics & SLOs.

Noah (VP Eng): From an eng POV, emphasize the runtime tradeoffs that customers can't easily reproduce: continuous batching, KV cache, smart routing across model variants. Those are the hard production problems. If we talk about "building models" we risk being compared to model providers; instead say we enable teams to serve models reliably.

Aisha (Strategy): Competitor shorthand we use in decks: "LLM API vendors" (convenience + models), "Inference infra" (self-hosted control), and "Cloud managed endpoints" (scale + lock-in). For messaging, call out the specific customer pain: unpredictable unit cost and flaky latency at scale — that's our hook.

Ellie (PM): Quick follow-up on GTM — should the playbook for Dedicated emphasize ROI math (committed throughput) or compliance features first when we talk to enterprises?

Morgan (CEO): Both, but ordering depends on the buyer. If they're cost-driven (ad networks, high-traffic apps) lead with ROI and predictable unit economics. If regulated (healthcare, finance) lead with private deployment, KMS/HSM, audit logs. Sales ops: we should add buyer persona snippets to playbooks.

Jordan (eng): Helpful — thanks. One more: when someone asks "why not just run on cloud GPUs ourselves?" what's the concise response?

Noah (VP Eng): Concise: we take on the ops and trade complexity for predictable results. Customers keep control of models but offload the infra lifecycle and optimizations that usually require a team of infra experts. Example elevator line: "You keep the model, we keep it fast and cheap to serve."

Aisha (Strategy): Also say: we provide observable economics — token-level cost + latency breakdowns — that's a tangible differentiator when teams compare.

Priya (Head of Product): Action item: I'll update the PLG landing copy to lead with "served inference economics" + a one-liner about hybrid deployments. Also prepping a one-pager for Sales with persona-first talking points.

Ellie (PM): Thanks everyone. If we can get the one-pager by EOD tomorrow that'd help the AE kickoff this week.

Morgan (CEO): Will prioritize. Appreciate the sharp questions — keep them coming in this thread or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
